definitions.explanation: Something happening without intention or planning; coincidentally.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{偶々|たまたま}⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{会|あ}った→会う：00482_au⟧。
examples.english: I happened to meet a friend at the station.

examples.japanese: {偶々|たまたま}⟦{通|とお}り→通る：01243_tooru⟧⟦かかった→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I shopped at a store I happened to pass by.

examples.japanese: {偶々|たまたま}⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦テレビ→テレビ：01536_terebi⟧⟦{番組|ばんぐみ}→番組：01705_bangumi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{面白|おもしろ}かった→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧。
examples.english: A TV program I happened to watch was interesting.

notes:
たまたま describes something happening by chance or coincidence, without planning or intention.

WRITING:
Almost always written in hiragana. The kanji {偶々|たまたま} exists but is rarely used.

USAGE:
Very common in everyday conversation. Typically placed before the verb or event that happened by chance.
- たまたま⟦{会|あ}った→会う：00482_au⟧: happened to meet
- たまたま⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧: happened to see
- たまたま⟦{通|とお}り→通る：01243_tooru⟧⟦かかった→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧: happened to pass by
たまたま carries no emotional weight — it simply states that something was unplanned. It can be used for both positive and negative coincidences.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たまたま: by chance (most natural in speech, emphasizes the randomness)
- ⟦{偶然|ぐうぜん}→偶然：02674_guuzen⟧: coincidentally (slightly more formal, can be used as a noun: ⟦{偶然|ぐうぜん}→偶然：02674_guuzen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一致|いっち}→一致：01733_icchi⟧ = coincidence)
- ⟦{思|おも}いがけず→思いがけず：07152_omoigakezu⟧: unexpectedly (emphasizes the surprise element)
